S&P 500 up 0.7%, Nasdaq up 0.8%; Bitcoin under $80k; Saudi power rates rise.
Armonia Capital
The Morning Balance · Tuesday, 27 October 2026

Today's balance

U.S. equity indices posted modest gains, with the S&P 500 at 7,676.77 and the Nasdaq at 26,169.38, while the dollar firmed and gold fell. The market remains balanced between equity strength and risk‑off pressure from the Bitcoin breach of $80,000 and heightened policy focus on utilities. The most immediate driver is Bitcoin’s dip below the $80,000 psychological level, prompting outflows from spot ETFs.

Market snapshot

SPX 7,676.77 USD ▲ 0.70%IXIC 26,169.38 USD ▲ 0.82%XAU 4,023.20 USD ▼ 0.38%DXY 102.22 USD ▲ 0.26%BTC 79,800.00 ▼ 0.68%ETH 2,313.27 ▼ 0.82%

Prices at the time of writing; may be delayed.

Top stories

Bitcoin dips below $80,000 as AI‑related sell‑off and Fed caution hit crypto markets
Prices fell to $79,280 on Oct 26 and traded at $80,000.3 on Oct 27, triggering $772.4 million withdrawals from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs. Source →

Saudi Arabia raises power and water tariffs for 2027
Residential rates rose 12 % from Oct 1 2024, lifting utility‑sector EBITDA forecasts by roughly 7 % and drawing interest from regional infrastructure funds. Source →

AI chip boom triples South Korea’s Q3 growth, implications for European supply chains
Samsung and SK Hynix are investing about €510 billion domestically, while the EU seeks small‑scale partnerships to access Korean HBM expertise. Source →

Morocco’s 2027 budget bill targets affordable rental housing for youth and students
The plan is backed by a sovereign‑bond issuance dedicated to real‑estate finance, signalling new opportunities for construction funding. Source →

Egypt signs $650 million solar power project agreements
Three 25‑year power‑purchase agreements for 2.5 GW of new solar capacity were signed, aimed at export to Gulf markets via a new “green hub”. Source →

Today's analysis

Bitcoin slips below $80,000 as AI sell‑off and Fed caution hit markets

Bitcoin’s dip below $80,000 reflects a clash between AI‑sector volatility, looming Fed policy and shifting ETF flows, reshaping the asset’s risk‑on equilibrium.

Read the full analysis →

Regional watch

Europe. South Korea’s AI‑chip surge could feed European data‑centre demand, prompting the EU to explore partnership pilots under Chips Act 2.0. Source →

Africa. Morocco’s housing budget creates a pipeline for construction financing, while the youth‑targeted scheme may influence regional real‑estate markets. Source →

Asia. The Reserve Bank of India released state‑government securities auction results, reflecting ongoing demand for domestic debt amid broader fiscal policy moves. Source →

MENA. Banque du Caire’s private‑tranche IPO is close to $4 billion, underscoring strong investor appetite for Gulf banking assets. Source →

What to watch today

  • Federal Reserve rate decision at 2 p.m. ET on Oct 31 2026 – a hawkish outcome could deepen Bitcoin’s sub‑$80k breach.
  • Net inflows/outflows in U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs for the week of Nov 4‑8 2026 – a shift to inflows would test support at $75 k.
  • Saudi utility earnings reports due after market close – data will gauge the impact of the 12 % tariff hike on sector profitability.

Featured asset of the day

Visa (V, stock)
Visa operates a global electronic payments network that authorises, clears and settles card‑based transactions, enabling merchants, banks and consumers to move money instantly and securely.

In focus today. The recent dip of Bitcoin below $80,000 has pressured crypto transaction volumes, directly affecting Visa’s emerging crypto‑payment services【4†L17-L20】.

Risks: Regulatory tightening on digital payments or stablecoins could limit Visa’s crypto‑related revenue streams. Competitive pressure from alternative payment networks and fintech platforms may erode Visa’s transaction volume growth.
